pages.text: Long before airplanes, brave sailors traveled across wide oceans in wooden ships.
Early ships were built from wood and powered by wind in large cloth sails.
Sailors learned to watch the stars at night to guide their direction.
The North Star helped many travelers know which way was north.
Ships carried spices, silk, gold, and other goods between distant lands.
These sea paths became trade routes that connected different continents.
When ships arrived in new places, people shared foods, tools, and ideas.
Explorers sometimes faced storms and strong waves during long journeys.
Careful navigation and teamwork helped ships reach faraway lands safely.
Ocean travel changed history by connecting cultures across the world.
